findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), a method that is not defined in UsernameForm, its superclass AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator/AbstractFormAuthenticator, or anywhere in this diff. The services module fails to compile: UsernameForm has no webauthnAuth field (that field belongs to UsernamePasswordForm) and no such method exists, so the entire build breaks and none of the PR's behavior or tests can run.

[BUG] badPasswordHandler() now calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context), but this diff adds no import of org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.util.AuthenticatorUtils to AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. If the class did not already import AuthenticatorUtils, the services module does not compile with a 'cannot find symbol' error; nothing in the shown import changes for this file introduces it.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate() calls this.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no such no-arg method exists in UsernameForm or any of its supertypes shown in the diff — the only isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) defined lives in UsernamePasswordForm, which is a sibling class, not a parent, so the file does not compile as diffed. The module fails to compile (or, if an identically-named method exists elsewhere out of diff, behavior is invisible here), and the passkeys-bypass of the user-set fast path in UsernameForm is untestable and unverifiable; the entire re-authentication fix for the UsernameForm flow cannot ship.

[ADVISORY] The re-authentication test asserts only the error message text after a failed password ('Invalid password.') and never asserts the symptom the production fix (setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError setting USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED) was written to correct — that the username stays fixed/hidden and registration is suppressed on the error page. A regression that reverts AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError to the old isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context) call (or drops the USERNAME_HIDDEN attribute) still passes this whole test suite, and the original bug — user able to change username during failed re-authentication — returns silently.

[ADVISORY] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError() call in createErrorResponse (the conditional-UI error path during re-authentication) has no test coverage anywhere in the diff — all three new re-auth tests exercise the success flow, and the reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test covers the UsernamePasswordForm error path, not the conditional-UI errorChallenge path. If createErrorResponse double-applies the form attributes (or the error page renders the username editable because fillContextForm re-runs after setError in the conditional authenticator), no test fails, and users mid-re-authentication with a failing passkey get a form where the username can be swapped — the exact class of bug this PR claims to fix.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled gates only on webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null, but never checks whether the user actually has a passkey/passwordless credential — yet the modified test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only exercises the realm-policy-disabled case, so the user-without-passkey-but-policy-enabled re-authentication rendering (fillContextForm producing a webauthn form with zero authenticators for that user) is unverified. A re-authenticating user with no passwordless credentials under a passkeys-enabled realm gets an empty/ghost 'authenticate with passkey' form on the error page; no test in this diff covers user!=null + policy on + no passkey credential, so a rendering regression there ships unnoticed.

[BUG] The challenge() guard inverts the previous user-null check: fillContextForm used to be invoked only when context.getUser() == null (initial login setting up conditional passkey UI on the username/password page), and the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so conditional-UI setup is skipped exactly in the case it was designed for. On the initial (non-re-auth) login error path — e.g. a user submits a wrong password on a passkey-enabled realm's username/password page — the WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm() else-branch that sets WebAuthnConstants.ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI and the username autocomplete script is never run, so the conditional passkey UI silently disappears from the error page after a first failed attempt, regressing the passwordless login flow this PR is not supposed to change.

[BUG] UsernameForm no longer skips the username step during re-authentication for ANY user whenever the realm has conditional passkeys enabled, regardless of whether that user actually possesses a webauthn credential. In realms using the separate UsernameForm execution with passkeys enabled, users who registered only a password (no passkey) lose the previous re-authentication skip: with prompt=login they are forced back to a username entry page and must retype their username even though the AuthenticationFlowContext already identifies them — a behavior change for non-passkey users that is not traceable to the stated intent (fixing passkey re-auth) and is untested (the new reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test only covers UsernamePasswordForm, not UsernameForm).

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning unconditional false in the conditional-UI subclass silently discards the authenticator-list rendering even when the user is identified and does have WebAuthn credentials, coupling the decision to authenticator subclassing rather than to user credential state. A future flow (or a custom subclass) that relies on WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator to show available authenticators during 2FA gets a hidden no-op; the base class contract documented as 'typically during 2-factor authentication' is overridden permanently for the entire conditional-UI family, making the next change to authenticator display require editing two parallel implementations.

[BUG] The negative assertion for the webauthn form is wrapped in try/catch (Exception), so it can never fail: driver.findElement throws NoSuchElementException when the form is absent (the expected case), and when the form IS present the assertThat(..., nullValue()) failure is an AssertionError, which is also caught by catch (Exception) and swallowed, making the whole check a no-op guard. The test 'reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey' stays green even if the webauthn form is wrongly rendered during password-only re-authentication (and on initial login), so a regression that re-introduces the passkey button for users without passkeys ships undetected.

[BUG] The second negative assertion for the webauthn form in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses the same try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception) pattern, which swallows both the NoSuchElementException (expected absence) and the AssertionError/fail() (unexpected presence), so the assertion is again a no-op. The re-authentication phase of the test cannot detect the webauthn form being incorrectly shown for a realm with passkeys disabled; the guard goes green while production behavior may be red.

[ADVISORY] The condition in challenge() was inverted from `context.getUser() == null` to `user != null`, so for an unidentified user's error challenge (e.g. wrong username on first login with passkeys enabled) fillContextForm is no longer called, dropping the conditional-UI webauthn attributes that the previous code set on that error page. Users on first-login error pages (wrong password typed before the browser autofill fired) lose the passkey conditional-UI prompt on the re-rendered challenge, degrading the passkey login experience in exactly the state the PR is about; the new tests only cover the identified-user error path, so this regression has no coverage.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is a confusable pair with the no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() invoked in UsernameForm.authenticate (UsernameForm.java:47): the two same-named predicates live in parent/child classes and gate the same user-set skip decision, so any future divergence in their definitions (e.g. one checking realm policy, the other not) silently desynchronizes the UsernameForm skip from the UsernamePasswordForm fill. The next editor changing one overload but not the other gets a flow where the username form is skipped (or shown) without the matching webauthn form setup, producing a blank or inconsistent re-authentication page; the parallel same-named predicates in two classes are the maintenance trap.

[BUG] UsernameForm calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist anywhere in its class hierarchy (the method added in this diff is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), and UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, not UsernamePasswordForm), so this diff does not compile. The build fails with a cannot-find-symbol error; even if a same-named method existed elsewhere, calling passkeys logic from a class that holds no webauthnAuth field signals copy-paste of intent without the supporting state.

[BUG] The guard for filling WebAuthn context data in authenticate() was silently inverted: the old code called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when the user was NOT yet selected (initial login), while the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so the initial-login path (user == null) no longer calls fillContextForm from authenticate(). First-visit username/password pages under a UsernamePasswordForm execution get their WebAuthn conditional-UI form data populated only if some other call site (e.g. challenge() or lazy form rendering) compensates; if it does not, the passkey autofill UI disappears on first login — a regression outside the PR's stated re-authentication objective with no test asserting the initial-page setup comes from this code path.

[ADVISORY] The test expectation for normal (non-re-auth) password login was flipped — previously the webauthn form was asserted ABSENT on the username/password page after username selection, now it is asserted PRESENT — documenting that this PR changes the ordinary login UX for passkey-enabled users, not just re-authentication. Users in organizations who type their username mid-flow now see a WebAuthn sign-in form on the password page where the prior release hid it; this is an intent expansion beyond the PR title 'Fixing Re-authentication with passkeys' and is only 'accepted' implicitly by rewriting the test, not by any explicit requirement in the diff.

[ADVISORY] During re-authentication (user already set in the auth context, e.g. prompt=login step-up), the UsernameForm no longer short-circuits to success when conditional passkeys are enabled, so the username entry form is rendered for an already-identified user with no visible enforcement in this diff that a subsequently submitted/selected identity must match the already-authenticated user. A step-up re-authentication session (e.g., admin console 'confirm identity' prompt) can be completed with a different username/passkey identity than the user the session was re-authenticating; any consumer relying on re-auth asserting the same principal (required actions, elevated admin operations) gets a silently switched identity. Admins configuring passkeys realms are bitten whenever the flow is used for step-up.

[ADVISORY] The negative webauthn-form check wraps an assertion and a fail() in a bare try/catch(Exception), making the fail('Not expected to have webauthn button') line unreachable dead code and the check's pass/fail logic opaque. A future maintainer changing the catch to `Throwable`, or swapping the matcher, gets a test that passes regardless of whether the webauthn form is rendered; also anyone reading the test cannot tell that the intended mechanism is 'findElement throws NoSuchElementException', and the identical copy-pasted block appears twice in this method, so a fix must be applied twice.

[BUG] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior (setting USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED form attributes after a failed re-authentication) is verified by no test in this diff — checked PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, which assert only error-message text ('Invalid password.'), info messages, and presence/absence of the `//form[@id='webauth']` element, never the hidden-username/registration-disabled form attributes. If setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError regresses (e.g., wrong auth-note key or Boolean.parseBoolean never true because the note is written elsewhere with different casing), the re-auth error page would show the username field and a registration link — the exact bug this PR claims to fix — while every test in the diff still passes green.

[BUG] The newly added AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call in createErrorResponse executes on the conditional-UI passkey-failure path, but no test in the diff triggers a failed conditional-UI passkey during re-authentication to exercise it — the three test files modified (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) only exercise successful passkey logins and failed *password* logins, never a passkey failure. A regression in the conditional-UI error branch (e.g., an exception or wrong form state when the auth note is absent on first login, since createErrorResponse also runs for non-re-auth failures) ships undetected; first-login passkey failures hitting this new code path have zero coverage.

[ADVISORY] In the second re-authentication round of webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, after prompt=login the test immediately logs in with the wrong password without asserting the login page or the 'Please re-authenticate to continue' info message, unlike the first round which asserts both. If the second prompt=login request skips the re-authentication page (e.g., due to a session-state regression where re-auth is silently satisfied), the incorrect-password login would go straight through and the subsequent Assert.assertEquals on the error message would fail with a confusing 'missing page' diagnosis instead of pinpointing the skipped re-auth step, and the wrong-password branch (which verifies the fix's error-path persistence of passkey UI) is only incidentally covered on the second round.

[BUG] challenge() now requires context.getUser() != null (via isConditionalPasskeysEnabled) to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm, so on a fresh login through UsernamePasswordForm where no user is set yet, the WebAuthn data that the previous `context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled()` branch produced is never populated. In a browser flow where UsernamePasswordForm runs without a prior user-selection step (e.g. UsernameForm is removed from the flow, or the user arrives with kerberos/IDP hint absent), the conditional-UI passkey script/challenge attributes are silently absent from the login page: the user sees a plain username/password form with no passkey autofill, no error is logged anywhere, and passkey login becomes unavailable on that flow even though the realm policy enables it.

[ADVISORY] During re-authentication, fillContextForm(context) is invoked twice for the same challenge — once in authenticate() and again inside challenge() — because both now fire when the user is set. The next change to fillContextForm's side effects (form attributes, authenticator lookup, session notes) has to reason about being applied twice per request; today it duplicates WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction and credential lookups on every re-authentication page render, a hot-path doubling of the DB-backed credential query.

The newly added/modified tests in the diff focus on successful re-authentication flows and, in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`, an incorrect-password error on the username/password form (not the conditional-UI `createErrorResponse` path). There is no test exercising a failing conditional-passkeys attempt during re-authentication to verify that `USERNAME_HIDDEN` / `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` attributes are correctly preserved on the rendered error page. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes passkeys UI population to run when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true (UsernamePasswordForm), which only checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null` and does not verify the user has any passwordless/WebAuthn credentials. While `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` does instantiate `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` and checks `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()`, the diff does not show what the empty-authenticator path renders (could hide or could leave a confusing UI), so the claimed “ghost form” can’t be proven from the diff. However, the finding’s core point is diff-grounded: no added/modified test covers the scenario `user != null` + realm passkeys enabled + user has no passkey credential during re-authentication; the new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` only covers the realm-policy-disabled case (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`), leaving that edge case unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes re-authentication behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate()`: it used to skip the form whenever `context.getUser() != null`, but now it skips only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (services/.../UsernameForm.java). That means enabling conditional passkeys can force the username step to be shown even though the user is already identified. However, from this diff alone we cannot verify the finding’s stronger claim that this happens “regardless of whether that user actually possesses a webauthn credential”, because the implementation/semantics of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` in `UsernameForm` is not shown here. The finding’s test-gap point is concrete: new re-authentication coverage was added for passkeys (e.g., `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), and for non-passkey reauth only in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, but there is no analogous non-passkey reauth test for the separate `UsernameForm` execution despite the behavior change in `UsernameForm`.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates rendering of the authenticator list on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (new method with default `return context.getUser() != null;`). `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that method to unconditionally `return false`, meaning the authenticator list will never be rendered for the conditional-UI variant even when `context.getUser()` is set. That behavior is explicit in the added override/comment, so it’s not a verifiable defect by itself, but it does introduce the architectural coupling the finding describes: future/custom uses of the conditional-UI subclass cannot show the list without editing/overriding this method again, diverging from the base-class “typically during 2-factor” contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The negative assertion for the webauthn form is wrapped in try/catch (Exception), so it can never fail: driver.findElement throws NoSuchElementException when the form is absent (the expected case), and when the form IS present the assertThat(..., nullValue()) failure is an AssertionError, which is also caught by catch (Exception) and swallowed, making the whole check a no-op guard. The test 'reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey' stays green even if the webauthn form is wrongly rendered during password-only re-authentication (and on initial login), so a regression that re-introduces the passkey button for users without passkeys ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the check is `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception ...) { /* expected */ }`. When the form is absent, `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` (an `Exception`) and the catch is reached (as intended). When the form is present, `findElement` returns a non-null `WebElement` and `assertThat(..., nullValue())` fails by throwing an `AssertionError`, which is an `Error` (not an `Exception`) and therefore is NOT swallowed by `catch (Exception)`. So the test would fail if the webauthn form is wrongly rendered; the guard is not a no-op as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second negative assertion for the webauthn form in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses the same try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception) pattern, which swallows both the NoSuchElementException (expected absence) and the AssertionError/fail() (unexpected presence), so the assertion is again a no-op. The re-authentication phase of the test cannot detect the webauthn form being incorrectly shown for a realm with passkeys disabled; the guard goes green while production behavior may be red.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the pattern `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception) {}` does not swallow `AssertionError` from `assertThat(..., nullValue())` or from `fail(...)` because the catch only handles `Exception`, while JUnit assertion failures throw `AssertionError` (an `Error`, not an `Exception`). If the element exists, the test will fail (assertion or fail) and will not be caught; if the element is absent, `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` (an `Exception`) and the catch treats it as expected. So the assertion is not a no-op as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The condition in challenge() was inverted from `context.getUser() == null` to `user != null`, so for an unidentified user's error challenge (e.g. wrong username on first login with passkeys enabled) fillContextForm is no longer called, dropping the conditional-UI webauthn attributes that the previous code set on that error page. Users on first-login error pages (wrong password typed before the browser autofill fired) lose the passkey conditional-UI prompt on the re-rendered challenge, degrading the passkey login experience in exactly the state the PR is about; the new tests only cover the identified-user error path, so this regression has no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)`, the condition to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` changed from `context.getUser() == null && ... isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a behavior inversion visible in the diff: when `context.getUser()` is null (e.g., initial/unknown-user state), the error challenge will no longer call `fillContextForm`, whereas it previously did. If `fillContextForm` is responsible for setting up the conditional-UI/passkeys-related form attributes, this would drop them on re-rendered error pages in the unidentified-user path. The added/modified tests shown focus heavily on re-authentication/identified-user scenarios and do not demonstrate coverage of the `context.getUser() == null` error-challenge path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is a confusable pair with the no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() invoked in UsernameForm.authenticate (UsernameForm.java:47): the two same-named predicates live in parent/child classes and gate the same user-set skip decision, so any future divergence in their definitions (e.g. one checking realm policy, the other not) silently desynchronizes the UsernameForm skip from the UsernamePasswordForm fill. The next editor changing one overload but not the other gets a flow where the username form is skipped (or shown) without the matching webauthn form setup, producing a blank or inconsistent re-authentication page; the parallel same-named predicates in two classes are the maintenance trap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two same-named predicates used to gate closely related behavior but defined differently: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now checks `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg method, defined elsewhere), while `UsernamePasswordForm` introduces `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` and uses it to decide when to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` (in both `authenticate()` and `challenge()`). This naming/overload mismatch across classes can plausibly confuse future edits (one predicate changed without the other), leading to inconsistent UI/flow decisions. It’s not a verifiable bug in this diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability hazard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist anywhere in its class hierarchy (the method added in this diff is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), and UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, not UsernamePasswordForm), so this diff does not compile. The build fails with a cannot-find-symbol error; even if a same-named method existed elsewhere, calling passkeys logic from a class that holds no webauthnAuth field signals copy-paste of intent without the supporting state.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UsernameForm.authenticate()` was changed to call `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg). The only `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` added by this PR is in `UsernamePasswordForm` and it has a different signature (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`). No no-arg method is added in `UsernameForm` or shown in its superclass (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`) in this diff, so based on the diff contents this introduces a likely `cannot find symbol` compilation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The guard for filling WebAuthn context data in authenticate() was silently inverted: the old code called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when the user was NOT yet selected (initial login), while the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so the initial-login path (user == null) no longer calls fillContextForm from authenticate(). First-visit username/password pages under a UsernamePasswordForm execution get their WebAuthn conditional-UI form data populated only if some other call site (e.g. challenge() or lazy form rendering) compensates; if it does not, the passkey autofill UI disappears on first login — a regression outside the PR's stated re-authentication objective with no test asserting the initial-page setup comes from this code path.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, both `authenticate()` and the error `challenge()` path changed from populating WebAuthn context whenever passkeys are enabled (and in `challenge()` explicitly when `context.getUser() == null`) to only doing so when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which requires `user != null` (new method at bottom of the class). This is a verifiable inversion for the initial-visit username/password page where the user is typically not yet set, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` will no longer be invoked from these code paths for `user == null`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test expectation for normal (non-re-auth) password login was flipped — previously the webauthn form was asserted ABSENT on the username/password page after username selection, now it is asserted PRESENT — documenting that this PR changes the ordinary login UX for passkey-enabled users, not just re-authentication. Users in organizations who type their username mid-flow now see a WebAuthn sign-in form on the password page where the prior release hid it; this is an intent expansion beyond the PR title 'Fixing Re-authentication with passkeys' and is only 'accepted' implicitly by rewriting the test, not by any explicit requirement in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does flip the normal login expectation and changes behavior beyond re-auth: in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest#passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey the assertion changes from WebAuthn form absent to present after username selection. This corresponds to UsernamePasswordForm now calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (i.e., user != null), whereas before it only filled WebAuthn data when context.getUser() == null. That is a UX/behavior scope expansion for ordinary username→password flows (user identified mid-flow), not just prompt=login re-authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] During re-authentication (user already set in the auth context, e.g. prompt=login step-up), the UsernameForm no longer short-circuits to success when conditional passkeys are enabled, so the username entry form is rendered for an already-identified user with no visible enforcement in this diff that a subsequently submitted/selected identity must match the already-authenticated user. A step-up re-authentication session (e.g., admin console 'confirm identity' prompt) can be completed with a different username/passkey identity than the user the session was re-authenticating; any consumer relying on re-auth asserting the same principal (required actions, elevated admin operations) gets a silently switched identity. Admins configuring passkeys realms are bitten whenever the flow is used for step-up.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` from short-circuiting whenever `context.getUser() != null` to only short-circuiting when `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (i.e., when conditional passkeys are enabled, the username step is no longer skipped even for an already-identified user). Nothing in this diff shows any added guard that the submitted username/passkey identity must match the pre-set `context.getUser()` for re-authentication/step-up scenarios; the only re-auth-related logic added (`AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`) merely hides username/registration on *error* forms and does not enforce principal immutability. This makes the finding's "identity switch during re-auth" concern a real, diff-grounded security/correctness regression risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The negative webauthn-form check wraps an assertion and a fail() in a bare try/catch(Exception), making the fail('Not expected to have webauthn button') line unreachable dead code and the check's pass/fail logic opaque. A future maintainer changing the catch to `Throwable`, or swapping the matcher, gets a test that passes regardless of whether the webauthn form is rendered; also anyone reading the test cannot tell that the intended mechanism is 'findElement throws NoSuchElementException', and the identical copy-pasted block appears twice in this method, so a fix must be applied twice.

[BUG] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior (setting USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED form attributes after a failed re-authentication) is verified by no test in this diff — checked PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, which assert only error-message text ('Invalid password.'), info messages, and presence/absence of the `//form[@id='webauth']` element, never the hidden-username/registration-disabled form attributes. If setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError regresses (e.g., wrong auth-note key or Boolean.parseBoolean never true because the note is written elsewhere with different casing), the re-auth error page would show the username field and a registration link — the exact bug this PR claims to fix — while every test in the diff still passes green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff refactors the re-authentication error-page setup into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (setting `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` parses to true), and calls it from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`. The added/modified tests (in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`, `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`) assert messages and presence/absence of the `//form[@id='webauth']` element, but do not assert that the username is hidden or registration is disabled on re-authentication errors. So a regression in this new logic could go undetected by the tests shown in the diff. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The newly added AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call in createErrorResponse executes on the conditional-UI passkey-failure path, but no test in the diff triggers a failed conditional-UI passkey during re-authentication to exercise it — the three test files modified (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, PasskeysUsernameFormTest, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) only exercise successful passkey logins and failed *password* logins, never a passkey failure. A regression in the conditional-UI error branch (e.g., an exception or wrong form state when the auth note is absent on first login, since createErrorResponse also runs for non-re-auth failures) ships undetected; first-login passkey failures hitting this new code path have zero coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call on the conditional-passkeys error path: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` now invokes `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` before `fillContextForm(context)`. The updated/added tests in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`, `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, and `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` exercise successful passkey logins and (in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`) failed password re-auth attempts, but none of them trigger the conditional-UI passkey failure path that would execute `createErrorResponse()`. That is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in coverage for newly added logic, though the code itself appears null-safe (`Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` => false), so it’s not a verifiable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In the second re-authentication round of webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, after prompt=login the test immediately logs in with the wrong password without asserting the login page or the 'Please re-authenticate to continue' info message, unlike the first round which asserts both. If the second prompt=login request skips the re-authentication page (e.g., due to a session-state regression where re-auth is silently satisfied), the incorrect-password login would go straight through and the subsequent Assert.assertEquals on the error message would fail with a confusing 'missing page' diagnosis instead of pinpointing the skipped re-auth step, and the wrong-password branch (which verifies the fix's error-path persistence of passkey UI) is only incidentally covered on the second round.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey(), the first re-auth round after prompt=login does `loginPage.assertCurrent();` and `assertEquals("Please re-authenticate to continue", loginPage.getInfoMessage());` before attempting the wrong-password login. In the second round, after `oauth.loginForm().prompt(...).open();` + `WaitUtils.waitForPageToLoad();`, it immediately calls `loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost"));` and asserts the error, without asserting the re-auth page/info message. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test robustness/diagnostic gap (not a product defect) because it weakens the test’s ability to pinpoint a regression where prompt=login does not show the expected re-auth UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] challenge() now requires context.getUser() != null (via isConditionalPasskeysEnabled) to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm, so on a fresh login through UsernamePasswordForm where no user is set yet, the WebAuthn data that the previous `context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled()` branch produced is never populated. In a browser flow where UsernamePasswordForm runs without a prior user-selection step (e.g. UsernameForm is removed from the flow, or the user arrives with kerberos/IDP hint absent), the conditional-UI passkey script/challenge attributes are silently absent from the login page: the user sees a plain username/password form with no passkey autofill, no error is logged anywhere, and passkey login becomes unavailable on that flow even though the realm policy enables it.
matched_golden_ids: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same regression: the conditional passkey/WebAuthn UI setup (via webauthnAuth.fillContextForm) is now gated on context.getUser() being non-null through isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so on the initial login form where no user is selected yet, the WebAuthn/conditional UI attributes are not populated, breaking ID-less/first-time passkey login flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] During re-authentication, fillContextForm(context) is invoked twice for the same challenge — once in authenticate() and again inside challenge() — because both now fire when the user is set. The next change to fillContextForm's side effects (form attributes, authenticator lookup, session notes) has to reason about being applied twice per request; today it duplicates WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction and credential lookups on every re-authentication page render, a hot-path doubling of the DB-backed credential query.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in two places in `UsernamePasswordForm`: once in `authenticate()` before calling `challenge(context, formData)`, and once in the error-path override `challenge(context, String error, String field)`. However, the finding’s core claim—"invoked twice for the same challenge" on re-authentication page render—is not verifiable from the diff: `authenticate()` calls the `challenge(context, MultivaluedMap...)` overload (whose body is not shown), while the second `fillContextForm` is only in the different `challenge(context, String, String)` overload. The diff does not show that the formData-based `challenge()` delegates to the error-based `challenge()` (or otherwise triggers a second `fillContextForm`) in the same request/render.
